title: Temporal role snapshots and member-impact heatmap for safe role edits
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Overview: Design a role editor surface that lets admins preview and validate permission changes before committing. Key innovations: 1) Temporal snapshots: view the role definition as it existed at a past date or across a range; 2) Member-impact heatmap: a visual summary showing how many users, teams, and resources would gain/lose access from a proposed change; 3) SSO/SAML mapping preview: overlay identity-provider group mappings and highlight mapping conflicts; 4) Audit-linked diffs: surface relevant audit log entries that explain why a permission was added/removed historically; 5) Safe-revert & dry-run flows: permit canary rollouts, dry-run simulations, and automated audit notes when a change is applied.

Goals: Reduce risky role edits and accidental privilege escalations by making consequences visible. Surface auditing context to accelerate incident reviews. Provide a fast, reversible workflow for admins with clear minimal friction for low-risk edits.

Design principles: 1) Deterministic previews — the UI must show exact effective permission deltas given current membership and group mappings; 2) Low-latency simulation — approximate results when full simulation is expensive, with a 'precise simulation' option; 3) Tie to audit & SSO — expose why a permission exists and how SSO mappings influence assignment; 4) Safety-first defaults — require explicit confirmation for high-risk changes and enable automatic canary policies.

Key screens & interactions:
- Role timeline panel: chronological slider to pick a snapshot date or compare two dates. Shows role attributes, description, assigned policies and last-modifier. 'Jump to audit' links to the audit event that created each change.
- Proposed change canvas: split view with 'Current' vs 'Proposed' role definitions and a highlighted permission delta list (added/removed/modified). Each permission line includes examples of affected resources and the reason (direct role membership vs inherited via group).
- Member-impact heatmap: matrix whose X axis is resource group (projects, datasets, deployments) and Y axis is member categories (users, groups, service accounts). Cells show counts and severity color (green/amber/red) indicating read/write/admin exposure. Hover shows sample user names and exact permission delta.
- SSO mapping overlay: shows which IdP groups map to the role and flags unmapped groups or conflicting rules. Provides a 'map suggestion' row based on heuristics and recent SAML assertions.
- Simulation & rollout controls: 'Dry run' to preview without changing live role; 'Canary' options to apply to a subset of users/groups; 'Auto-revert threshold' to rollback rollouts that trigger elevated error rates or sensitive telemetry.

Telemetry & backend constraints (for engineering): Need an efficient permission simulation API that accepts: role delta + snapshot date + optional IDP mapping state and returns counts and sample principals. Strict time budget: initial preview should return within 1s for typical orgs; fall back to cached approximations with clear UI messaging. This introduces trade-offs: sample-based heatmap vs exhaustive simulation; we must expose confidence and sample size.

Accessibility & copy notes: Use clear labels (e.g., 'May gain write access', 'May lose access') and avoid jargon. Add inline help for 'Canary' and 'Dry run'. Ensure keyboard navigation for the heatmap and ARIA labels for color semantics.

Out-of-scope for initial rollout: per-resource granular simulations for >100k resources; fine-grained cost estimation for access changes.

Acceptance criteria:
- Wireframes for all key screens (timeline, proposed change canvas, heatmap, SSO overlay) delivered and reviewed by PM and Eng.
- Simulation API contract documented and agreed by ENG team (latency SLOs, fallback behavior).
- Usability test with at least 6 admins showing >80% task success on previewing and reverting a risky change.
- Security review completed and hard-block gating for high-risk changes implemented.
